diagnosis: Multiple chondromas in a patient with Carney triad
legend: Gross photo showing multiple well-circumscribed nodules. Most of these nodules are calcified and ossified, with a pale-grey, gritty cut surface. One nodule, mainly composed of cartilage, has a whiter and smoother cut surface.

diagnosis: Multiple chondromas in a patient with Carney triad
legend: Chondroma is mostly composed of cartilage, with focal calcification and ossification. Note the well-circumscribed contour, with no invagination, in contrast to hamartoma.

diagnosis: Multiple chondromas in a patient with Carney triad
legend: Although the cartilage is typically hyaline, myxoid changes are often seen and can occasionally be prominent.

diagnosis: Multiple chondromas in a patient with Carney triad
legend: When ossification occurs, it is often associated with prominent adipose tissue, as would be seen in bone marrow. This is to be distinguished from the adipose tissue seen in hamartoma.
Chondroma (WSI) arising in Carney's complex patient.
